title: No Longer Human
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Junji Ito's three-volume adaptation of Osamu Dazai's novel follows Yozo Oba, a man who from childhood feels unable to understand other people and hides behind clowning. His life spirals through abuse in childhood, womanizing, alcohol, morphine addiction and suicide attempts. Ito adds horror imagery to show Yozo's inner world.
life_message: A tragedy rather than a model: it shows a man destroyed by alienation, shame and self-destruction, and leaves readers to ask what might have saved him.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Yozo drifts outside family, work and social rules.

folkways.japan: The novel is a canonical work of Japanese literature, and its themes of shame (haji) and the masks people wear in a conformist society are central to how it is read in Japan.
